name: Nearby Bluetooth devices
plain: Sites cannot scan for nearby Bluetooth devices without a picker you approve.
meaning: Web Bluetooth (Chromium) requires a user gesture, a chooser prompt and a service filter; the page only gets devices the person picks. Silent scanning does not exist. Safari and Firefox do not support Web Bluetooth.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: proxy: requestDevice filters
fields.range: page sees only the chosen device

limits.headline: Can't scan for nearby Bluetooth devices without a picker you approve
limits.user_action: You tap Connect device and pick one from the browser list
can: Ask to connect to one device in Chrome or Edge on Android and desktop
Show a list for you to choose from
Work with the one device you pick, for that visit
cannot: See the list of devices you did not pick
Work in Safari, Firefox, or on iPhone
Keep a device linked forever without asking again
limits.differs: Web Bluetooth works in Chromium browsers only. Safari and Firefox do not offer it.

story.what_it_is: Sites cannot scan for Bluetooth devices around you without a picker you approve.

marketing.name: Web Bluetooth
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes a way to talk to a nearby Bluetooth device after you choose it from a list.

story.for_you: A site cannot quietly list your earbuds, watch or other gadgets. If it wants to connect, Chrome shows a chooser and you pick one device. Safari does not offer it at all.
story.for_makers: Apps wanted to scan for nearby devices to find shoppers in stores, to track people or to set up gadgets. The web allows only a user-chosen device, so these uses are blocked. Real gadget setup uses the picker.

use_cases.example: A smart light site wants to find every bulb nearby, but must wait for you to pick one in the chooser.
A heart rate chest strap page wants to connect, and you choose your strap in the picker.
A device maker's setup page uses the picker to flash firmware onto one device.
A store app wanted to detect shoppers by phone signals, which a web page cannot do.
A browser game wanted to find nearby friends' phones, but can only use the picker or a code.
A tracker wanted to log which Bluetooth gadgets you carry to recognise you, which is blocked.
A blood sugar monitor page connects to the one sensor you pick.

risks: Picker can still be tapped by mistake

legit_uses: None: the browser deliberately withholds it
abuse: Beacon based indoor tracking in native apps
